correctness.rationale: Discrete Fourier transform splits the 2d normalized kernel Gram matrix into d Hermitian 2x2 blocks with A_k=d r^(2k)F_k(r^(2d)), B_k=d s^(2k)F_k(s^(2d)), mixed modulus |C_k|=d(rs)^k|F_k((rs)^d e^(-id theta))|. Their strictly positive determinants multiply with (1-r²)^(pd)(1-s²)^(pd). The Veronese numerator recurrence gives positive coefficients, correct degree and simple negative real roots by Sturm-style sign interlacing; Jochemko establishes broader real-rootedness prior, so no novelty claimed for it. Numerator |w+a|² increases and |1-w| denominator decreases strictly with u=1+cos(d theta), forcing each block determinant and product to decrease strictly in u including duplicate-point endpoint. Independent direct determinant/phase checks verified 64 cases across p=2..5,d=2..5; proof applies all p,d≥2 and 0<r,s<1.
residual_risks: Fixed 0<r,s<1, p,d positive integers at least two, equal-cardinality regular orbits; optimization only over relative angle, not orbit radii or arbitrary node placements.
